clue.text: Pain evident, as smoker has to take oxygen

parts.note: a lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney, which smokes
to bag something is to take or seize it
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A smoker in visible pain has to be given oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is Scots for a chimney, the 'smoker' here, not a person with a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is a dull ache in the lower back, a specific kind of bodily pain.

clue.text: Retreat when Orwell's guillotined

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the surname is cut off

parts.note: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair

explanation.surface: Someone retreats when the writer Orwell has his head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' removes the head of BLAIR, Orwell's real surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hideaway, a place of retreat.

clue.text: Unlikely James IV of Scotland unknown -— this his title

indicators.note: an unlikely version of a name is a scrambled one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: IV is the Roman numeral four, so the fourth letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, as in x and y

explanation.surface: King James IV of Scotland was given a royal title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' rearranges JAMES into MAJES; 'IV of' takes the fourth letter, T, of Scotland. The surface reads IV as the king's number.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is formally addressed as Your Majesty, so it was the Scottish king's title.

clue.text: Strength shown when firm

parts.note: as can mean while or when
set means firm or solid, like set jelly

explanation.surface: A company's strength is on display when it is firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it means solid, SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, a strong point.

clue.text: Eastern time in North America, passing through college

indicators.note: the American piece goes right inside the college name

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

indicators.note: the time letter sits inside the continent abbreviation

explanation.surface: Eastern time in North America is mentioned while passing through a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside NA to give NTA, which 'passing through' places inside ORIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the Orient, the East, so it is a synonym of eastern.

clue.text: First of riders on horseback goes on to rouse his supporter?

indicators.note: the following pieces are attached after the synonym for rouse

parts.note: to rouse someone is to stir them

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word riders is taken

parts.note: a jockey who is up is mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: A leading rider in the saddle goes on to stir up a supporter of his.
explanation.walkthrough: R (first of 'riders') with UP (mounted) 'goes on to' STIR. The question mark flags that 'his' refers back to the rider, whose foot is held by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in this metal loop hung from the saddle, so it supports him.

clue.text: Read article, and be incensed

parts.note: to read a situation is to see or understand it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads an article and becomes furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, like a pot simmering, which is being incensed.

clue.text: By that very cheap type of bed, replace cot

annotationWithheld.why: By that very cheap type of bed, replace cot (4,5): the letters are an anagram of PI (type) + SOFA (bed) + COT, but 'cheap' then has no job, and no parse found gives it one
annotationWithheld.clue: By that very cheap type of bed, replace cot

clue.text: Maintained high position, though fell, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for fell is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rain fell means it rained

explanation.surface: Someone kept a high position though they had a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a stumble, but here it is rain falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigned held the throne, the highest position, for that time.

clue.text: Spray foot sore which is hot

definitions.note: a relative phrase standing for a thing that is hot

parts.note: to pepper something is to spray it with shot or small missiles
a corn is a hard painful patch on the foot

explanation.surface: Spraying a sore foot makes it burn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried black pepper berry is pungent and spicy, so it is something hot to the taste.

clue.text: It's unfair to get in the way, plugging fruity extract

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the road abbreviation stops up the middle of the fruit word, like a plug

parts.note: juice is the liquid extracted from fruit
ST, short for street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Getting in someone's way while squeezing fruit juice is simply not fair.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is a common abbreviation for street, here 'the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: An injustice is something unfair, so the clue's phrase stands in for the noun.

clue.text: Lose the fat, given pressure to tighten one's belt

parts.note: to skim milk is to take the cream or fat off it
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone dieting under pressure loses weight and tightens their belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise or spend sparingly, idiomatically tightening one's belt.

clue.text: Survey two gardens, but don't choose either?

definitions.text: Survey two gardens, but don't choose either?

parts.words: Survey two gardens, but don't choose either?
parts.note: someone perched on the boundary between two gardens can look over both, and the same perch is the idiom for refusing to take a side

explanation.surface: A neighbour looks over two gardens and won't pick one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay neutral, literally perched on the boundary between two plots.

clue.text: The unravelling of a yarn

parts.note: reads like wool coming undone, but yarn means a story and unravelling means the plot's final untangling

explanation.surface: A ball of wool comes undone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from French for untying a knot and names the final resolution of a story's plot.

clue.text: Mummy will be given drug, then pain ain't bad

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

indicators.note: bad letters are ones put in a broken order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A mummy is given drugs, and then the pain is not so bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges AINT into TIAN. GYP is British slang for pain or discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptian dead were preserved as mummies, so a mummy is typically from that country.

clue.text: Spot deal, perhaps, with any luck

parts.note: a spot or a touch is a small amount, as in a touch of rain
deal is a soft timber such as pine, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A gambler spots a deal and hopes for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a bargain, but it is pine or fir timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this phrase, while tapping timber, is a superstitious hope for good fortune.

clue.text: Openings of all concerti ideally delivered in C sharp

indicators.note: the first letter of each following word is taken, as an opening is a start

explanation.surface: Concerti are ideally delivered in the key of C sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of every word from 'all' to 'C' is taken; 'sharp' is left over as the definition, not part of the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic tastes are tart or sour, which is what sharp means of flavour.

clue.text: Writer about to correspend in colour

indicators.note: the pen goes around the other word

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the paper's misprint for to correspond, and to correspond is to agree or match

explanation.surface: A writer is about to write letters in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper printed 'correspend', a slip for 'correspond'. 'about' puts AGREE inside PEN; 'correspond' looks like writing letters but here means to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a shade of light yellowish green, the colour of peas.

clue.text: Loathsome party backtracking with promises

indicators.note: going back means the word for party is read right to left

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A party backtracks on its promises, which is loathsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, a direct synonym of loathsome.

clue.text: Repeat that which was mentioned before English class

indicators.note: before places the pronoun ahead of the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: the pronoun it refers back to something already mentioned
rate means a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A teacher repeats what was said before an English class.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, a formal synonym of repeat.

clue.text: They would fight to get naked female on back, along with me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the three pieces before it are read as one run backwards

parts.note: raw can mean bare or naked, as in a raw wound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fighting men are tempted by a naked woman lying on her back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAW + F + ON into NOFWAR, and ME goes in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Men-of-war are warships, armed vessels built to fight.

clue.text: A far from cryptic acronym?

parts.note: an initialism from computing for a screen that shows exactly what will print, so nothing is hidden

explanation.surface: An acronym that is anything but puzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: The computing initialism stands for what you see is what you get, the opposite of hidden meaning.

clue.text: Oxford's content to be rude when short of books

indicators.note: lacking means the books abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: insolent means rude or cheeky
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: An Oxford student is happy to be rude when without books.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a type of laced shoe, so its content is the inner sole, not a university's.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a laced shoe, and the inner sole lies inside it.

clue.text: Size of paper shop offering source of paper

parts.note: elephant is an old British size of drawing paper
to shop someone is to inform on them, which is also to grass

explanation.surface: A stationer's shop offers paper of a certain size.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'shop' and 'grass' are British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall African grass is a fibre source used in papermaking.

clue.text: Growth of Colorado ski resort?

definitions.meaning: a tree is a growth, and this is a poplar
a famous ski town in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado

explanation.surface: Something grows in a Colorado ski town.
explanation.definitionFit: The ski town is named after the quaking poplar trees growing around it.

clue.text: Part raised in Ireland, as it was known

definitions.text: Part raised in Ireland, as it was known

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
only part of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Part of something was raised in Ireland long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' takes NIRE from 'in Ireland' and 'raised' turns it upwards; the clue as a whole also describes the old poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old poetic name for Ireland, from the Irish Éire.

clue.text: Long time needed to find poetical inspiration

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet takes ages to find inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is one of the nine Muses in Greek myth, the one for lyric and love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: This Muse is the goddess who inspires lyric poetry, so she is poetical inspiration.

clue.text: Defeat, or we prove to be beaten

indicators.note: beaten as with eggs: the letters are whisked into a new order

explanation.surface: We prove that we can be beaten, which is a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be beaten' rearranges the letters of OR WE PROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower an opponent is to defeat them by greater strength.

clue.text: Lever related to switch

indicators.note: switching letters means swapping them round into a new order

explanation.surface: A lever is related to a switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch' rearranges RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: Figure it's high time horse is shackled

indicators.note: the horse is held inside the time word, like a prisoner in chains

parts.note: noon is when the sun is at its highest
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: It is high time a horse was fettered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shackled' puts NAG inside NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric figure with nine sides.
